import Cryptography.TypeChannelMilestone.InfoCalculus

/-!
# The Galois/Frobenius side channel: data processing and the independence law

This file strengthens two of the three closures of the Galois/Frobenius side-channel
family (`Cryptography.NonabelianTypeChannel.*`, the which-factor wall and the
Artin/torsor channel) from *support / one-readout* statements to *distributional,
all-post-processings* statements, in the finite Shannon calculus of
`Cryptography.NonabelianTypeChannel.Entropy`.

## Main results

* `mutualInfo_comp_left_le`, `mutualInfo_comp_both_le` — **data processing**:
  post-processing either readout never increases a channel.
* `residue_postprocess_le_index` — the **abelianization cap for every post-processed
  residue readout**: `I(ψ ∘ coset ; φ ∘ T) ≤ I(coset ; T) ≤ log₂ [S : N]`.  The catalog
  cap `typeChannel_le_logb_index` only covered the coset readout itself and injective
  relabellings of it (`residue_channel_eq_coset_channel`).
* `mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_card_mul` — the **independence law** in counting form: if every
  joint cell count factors, the channel is exactly zero.
* `frobenius_one_time_pad` — **the Artin channel is a one-time pad**: in *any* finite
  Galois group `S` (abelian or not), for any candidate set `A ⊆ S` of Frobenius elements
  of `p` and a Chebotarev-uniform Frobenius of `q` in `S`, *every* readout of the
  product `σ_p σ_q` carries
  **exactly zero** bits about *every* readout of `σ_p`.
* `frobenius_posterior_eq_prior` — the same, as "posterior = prior": conditioning on any
  observed value of the product readout leaves the law of every readout of `σ_p`
  unchanged.  This is the distributional strengthening of `nonabelian_no_pruning`
  (which only says the posterior has full *support*).
* `frobenius_pad_breaks_with_cofactor` — non-vacuity: once the Frobenius of the cofactor
  is also revealed, the product readout carries the full `log₂ |A|` bits.
-/

namespace TypeChannel

namespace GaloisSideChannel

open Finset Real

variable {Ω α β γ δ : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [DecidableEq δ]

/-! ## 1. Data processing -/

/-- **Data processing (left).**  Post-processing the first readout by any function `ψ`
never increases the channel: `I(ψ ∘ f ; g) ≤ I(f ; g)`. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comp_left_le (S : Finset Ω) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) (ψ : α → γ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun w => ψ (f w)) g ≤ mutualInfo S f g := by
  rw [mutualInfo_comm S _ g, mutualInfo_comm S f g]
  calc mutualInfo S g (fun w => ψ (f w))
      ≤ mutualInfo S g (pairObs (fun w => ψ (f w)) f) := mutualInfo_le_pair g _ f
    _ = mutualInfo S g f := by
        rw [mutualInfo_comm S g, mutualInfo_comm S g f]
        refine mutualInfo_congr_partition (c := f) (c' := pairObs (fun w => ψ (f w)) f) g ?_
        intro a _ b _
        simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq]
        constructor
        · intro h; exact ⟨by rw [h], h⟩
        · exact fun h => h.2

/-- **Data processing (right).** `I(f ; φ ∘ g) ≤ I(f ; g)`. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comp_right_le (S : Finset Ω) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) (φ : β → δ) :
    mutualInfo S f (fun w => φ (g w)) ≤ mutualInfo S f g := by
  rw [mutualInfo_comm S f _, mutualInfo_comm S f g]
  exact mutualInfo_comp_left_le S g f φ

/-- **Data processing (both sides).** `I(ψ ∘ f ; φ ∘ g) ≤ I(f ; g)`. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comp_both_le (S : Finset Ω) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) (ψ : α → γ)
    (φ : β → δ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun w => ψ (f w)) (fun w => φ (g w)) ≤ mutualInfo S f g :=
  (mutualInfo_comp_right_le S _ g φ).trans (mutualInfo_comp_left_le S f g ψ)

section Residue

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] {κ τ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] [DecidableEq τ]

/-- **The abelianization cap for every post-processed residue readout.**  Let `S` be a
finite Galois group, `N` its derived subgroup and `c` the coset (residue-class) readout.
For *any* coarsening `ψ` of the residue (e.g. reducing `p` to a smaller modulus, or
any arithmetic function of the residue) and *any* post-processing `φ` of the splitting
type, the channel is bounded by the coset channel, and hence by `log₂ [S : N]`. -/
theorem residue_postprocess_le_index {S N : Finset G} {c : G → κ}
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hN : IsSubgroupFinset N) (hNS : N ⊆ S)
    (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c) (T : G → τ) (ψ : κ → γ) (φ : τ → δ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun g => ψ (c g)) (fun g => φ (T g)) ≤ mutualInfo S c T ∧
      mutualInfo S c T ≤ logb 2 (S.image c).card :=
  ⟨mutualInfo_comp_both_le S c T ψ φ, typeChannel_le_logb_index hS hN hNS hc T⟩

omit [DecidableEq G] in
/-- In a perfect Galois group *every* post-processed residue readout leaks exactly
nothing about *every* post-processed type readout. -/
theorem residue_postprocess_eq_zero_of_perfect {S : Finset G} {c : G → κ}
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hc : IsCosetReadout S S c) (T : G → τ) (ψ : κ → γ)
    (φ : τ → δ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun g => ψ (c g)) (fun g => φ (T g)) = 0 := by
  have h1 := mutualInfo_comp_both_le S c T ψ φ
  rw [typeChannel_eq_zero_of_perfect hS hc T] at h1
  have h2 := mutualInfo_nonneg (S := S) ⟨1, hS.one_mem⟩ (fun g => ψ (c g)) (fun g => φ (T g))
  linarith

end Residue

/-! ## 2. The independence law -/

/-- **The independence law (probability form).**  If the joint law of `(f, g)` is the
product of the marginals on the product of the images, the channel is exactly zero. -/
theorem mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_prob_mul {S : Finset Ω} {f : Ω → α} {g : Ω → β}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ S.image f, ∀ b ∈ S.image g,
      prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b) = prob S f a * prob S g b) :
    mutualInfo S f g = 0 := by
  rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hS | hS
  · subst hS; simp [mutualInfo, entropy]
  have hpair : entropy S (pairObs f g) = entropy S f + entropy S g := by
    rw [entropy_eq_sum_of_subset (image_pairObs_subset (S := S) (f := f) (g := g)),
      Finset.sum_product]
    have hterm : ∀ a ∈ S.image f, ∑ b ∈ S.image g,
        -(prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b) * logb 2 (prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b)))
          = -(prob S f a * logb 2 (prob S f a)) * ∑ b ∈ S.image g, prob S g b
            + prob S f a * ∑ b ∈ S.image g, -(prob S g b * logb 2 (prob S g b)) := by
      intro a ha
      rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun b hb => ?_)
      rw [h a ha b hb, Real.logb_mul (prob_pos_of_mem ha).ne' (prob_pos_of_mem hb).ne']
      ring
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_add_distrib, sum_prob hS]
    simp only [mul_one]
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, sum_prob hS, one_mul]
    rfl
  unfold mutualInfo
  rw [hpair]; ring

/-- A joint cell count that factors gives a joint probability that factors. -/
lemma prob_pair_eq_mul_of_card_mul {S : Finset Ω} {f : Ω → α} {g : Ω → β} {a : α} {b : β}
    (hS : S.Nonempty)
    (h : (fiber S (pairObs f g) (a, b)).card * S.card = (fiber S f a).card * (fiber S g b).card) :
    prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b) = prob S f a * prob S g b := by
  have hS' : (S.card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr hS).ne'
  have hc : ((fiber S (pairObs f g) (a, b)).card : ℝ) * S.card
      = (fiber S f a).card * (fiber S g b).card := by exact_mod_cast h
  unfold prob
  field_simp
  linarith

/-- **The independence law (counting form).**  If every joint cell count satisfies
`#{f = a, g = b} · |S| = #{f = a} · #{g = b}`, the channel is exactly zero. -/
theorem mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_card_mul {S : Finset Ω} {f : Ω → α} {g : Ω → β}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ S.image f, ∀ b ∈ S.image g,
      (fiber S (pairObs f g) (a, b)).card * S.card = (fiber S f a).card * (fiber S g b).card) :
    mutualInfo S f g = 0 := by
  refine mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_prob_mul (fun a ha b hb => ?_)
  obtain ⟨w, hw, _⟩ := mem_image.mp ha
  exact prob_pair_eq_mul_of_card_mul ⟨w, hw⟩ (h a ha b hb)

/-! ## 3. The Artin channel is a one-time pad -/

section OneTimePad

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] {S A : Finset G}

/-- The counting core of the one-time pad: inside a finite Galois group `S`, the shear
`(x, z) ↦ (x, x⁻¹ z)` identifies the cell `{F x = a, H (x y) = b}` of `A × S` with a
product of a cell of `F` on `A` and a cell of `H` on `S`. -/
lemma card_shear_filter (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (P Q : G → Prop)
    [DecidablePred P] [DecidablePred Q] :
    ((A ×ˢ S).filter (fun z => P z.1 ∧ Q (z.1 * z.2))).card
      = (A.filter P).card * (S.filter Q).card := by
  have hset : (A ×ˢ S).filter (fun z => P z.1 ∧ Q (z.1 * z.2))
      = ((A.filter P) ×ˢ (S.filter Q)).image (fun u : G × G => (u.1, u.1⁻¹ * u.2)) := by
    ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_product, mem_image, Prod.mk.injEq, Prod.exists]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨hx, hy⟩, hP, hQ⟩
      exact ⟨x, x * y, ⟨⟨hx, hP⟩, hS.mul_mem _ (hA hx) _ hy, hQ⟩, rfl, by group⟩
    · rintro ⟨u, v, ⟨⟨hu, hP⟩, hv, hQ⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨⟨hu, hS.mul_mem _ (hS.inv_mem _ (hA hu)) _ hv⟩, hP, ?_⟩
      simpa using hQ
  rw [hset, Finset.card_image_of_injective, Finset.card_product]
  intro u v huv
  simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at huv
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := huv
  refine Prod.ext h1 ?_
  rw [h1] at h2
  exact mul_left_cancel h2

/-- The cell counts of the product channel factor exactly:
`#{F x = a, H (x y) = b} · |A × S| = #{F x = a} · #{H (x y) = b}`. -/
lemma pad_card_mul (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (F : G → α) (H : G → β)
    (a : α) (b : β) :
    (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (pairObs (fun z : G × G => F z.1)
      (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2))) (a, b)).card * (A ×ˢ S).card
      = (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => F z.1) a).card *
        (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b).card := by
  have h1 : (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (pairObs (fun z : G × G => F z.1)
      (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2))) (a, b)).card
      = (A.filter (fun x => F x = a)).card * (S.filter (fun x => H x = b)).card := by
    rw [← card_shear_filter hS hA]
    unfold fiber pairObs
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq]
  have h2 : (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => F z.1) a).card
      = (A.filter (fun x => F x = a)).card * (S.filter (fun _ => True)).card := by
    rw [← card_shear_filter hS hA]
    unfold fiber
    simp only [and_true]
  have h3 : (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b).card
      = (A.filter (fun _ => True)).card * (S.filter (fun x => H x = b)).card := by
    rw [← card_shear_filter hS hA]
    unfold fiber
    simp only [true_and]
  rw [h1, h2, h3, Finset.card_product]
  simp only [filter_true]
  ring

/-- **The Artin channel is a one-time pad.**  Let `S` be a finite (possibly non-abelian)
Galois group.  Model the Frobenius of `p` as uniform on an arbitrary candidate set
`A ⊆ S` and the Frobenius of `q` as uniform on `S` (Chebotarev).  Then *any* readout `H`
of the Frobenius of `N`, `σ_N = σ_p σ_q` — its conjugacy class, its abelianization coset,
its cycle type, anything — carries **exactly zero** bits about *any* readout `F` of
`σ_p`. -/
theorem frobenius_one_time_pad (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (F : G → α)
    (H : G → β) :
    mutualInfo (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => F z.1) (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2)) = 0 :=
  mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_card_mul (fun a _ b _ => pad_card_mul hS hA F H a b)

/-- **Posterior equals prior.**  For every observed value `b` of the readout of the
Frobenius of `N`, the conditional law of every readout of the Frobenius of `p` equals its
prior law.  `nonabelian_no_pruning` is the support shadow of this statement. -/
theorem frobenius_posterior_eq_prior (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (F : G → α)
    (H : G → β) (a : α) {b : β} (hb : b ∈ (A ×ˢ S).image (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2))) :
    prob (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2)) b) (fun z => F z.1) a
      = prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => F z.1) a := by
  have hpb : 0 < prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b := prob_pos_of_mem hb
  obtain ⟨w, hw, _⟩ := mem_image.mp hb
  have hjoint := prob_pair_eq_mul_of_card_mul ⟨w, hw⟩ (pad_card_mul hS hA F H a b)
  have hchain := prob_pair_eq_mul (S := A ×ˢ S) (X := fun z : G × G => F z.1)
    (t := fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) (a := a) hb
  rw [hjoint] at hchain
  have key : prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b *
      (prob (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b) (fun z => F z.1) a
        - prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => F z.1) a) = 0 := by
    rw [mul_sub]; linarith
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp key with h | h
  · exact absurd h hpb.ne'
  · linarith

/-- **Non-vacuity: the pad breaks once the cofactor's Frobenius is revealed.**  The pair
(Frobenius of `N`, Frobenius of `q`) determines the Frobenius of `p`, so it carries the
full `log₂ |A|` bits about it.  The zero of `frobenius_one_time_pad` is therefore a
genuine independence phenomenon, not an entropy deficit. -/
theorem frobenius_pad_breaks_with_cofactor (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S)
    (hA0 : A.Nonempty) :
    mutualInfo (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => z.1) (fun z => (z.1 * z.2, z.2)) = logb 2 A.card := by
  rw [mutualInfo_eq_left_of_factors (φ := fun u : G × G => u.1 * u.2⁻¹)
    (fun w _ => by simp)]
  have himg : (A ×ˢ S).image (fun z : G × G => z.1) = A := by
    ext x
    simp only [mem_image, mem_product, Prod.exists, exists_and_right, exists_eq_right]
    exact ⟨fun ⟨_, h, _⟩ => h, fun h => ⟨1, h, hS.one_mem⟩⟩
  rw [entropy_eq_logb_card_of_uniform_fibers (k := S.card)
    (hA0.product ⟨1, hS.one_mem⟩) (card_pos.mpr ⟨1, hS.one_mem⟩), himg]
  intro x hx
  rw [himg] at hx
  have := card_shear_filter hS hA (fun y => y = x) (fun _ => True)
  simp only [and_true, filter_true] at this
  unfold fiber
  rw [this, Finset.filter_eq' A x, if_pos hx, card_singleton, one_mul]

end OneTimePad

/-!
# The which-factor wall for Galois groups, for any number of prime factors

The catalog's which-factor wall (`CyclicTypeChannel.whichFactor_wall`,
`Combinatorics/D12SemiprimeWhichFactorWall.lean`) is stated for the cyclic exponent box
of `Q(ζ_ℓ)` and for a *binary* label.  This file lifts it to

* an **abstract symmetry wall** (`symmetry_wall`): whenever the readout-preserving
  symmetries of the sample space act transitively on the values of a label `w`, the
  label is *exactly* uniform (`log₂ #labels` bits) and *every* readout preserved by those
  symmetries carries *exactly* zero bits about it;
* the **Galois semiprime wall** (`galois_whichFactor_wall`) over an *arbitrary*, possibly
  non-abelian, finite Galois group, with the key arithmetic input proved rather than
  assumed: the residue class of `N = p q` (the abelianization coset of `σ_p σ_q`) and
  more generally every class function of `σ_p σ_q` is swap-invariant
  (`classFn_mul_swap`, `cosetReadout_isClassFn`), so the full readout
  (residue of `N`, unordered type pair) hides the which-factor bit completely
  (`residue_and_types_hide_whichFactor`);
* the **multi-prime wall** (`multiFactor_wall`): for `N = p₀ ⋯ p_m` with pairwise
  distinct splitting types, *which of the `m+1` factors carries the smallest type* is a
  label of exactly `log₂ (m+1)` bits, and every readout invariant under transposing two
  factors carries exactly zero bits about it.

Each wall is shown non-vacuous: the *ordered* readout recovers the whole label
(`galois_whichFactor_ordered_full`, `multiFactor_ordered_full`).
-/

namespace TypeChannel

namespace GaloisSideChannel

open Finset Real

variable {Ω α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]

/-! ## 1. The abstract symmetry wall -/

section Abstract

variable {S : Finset Ω} {w : Ω → α} {k : Ω → β}

/-- The hypothesis of the symmetry wall: for any two label values in use there is a
bijection of the sample space preserving the readout `k` and carrying the first label
class onto the second. -/
def LabelTransitive (S : Finset Ω) (w : Ω → α) (k : Ω → β) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ S.image w, ∀ b ∈ S.image w, ∃ σ : Ω → Ω,
    Set.BijOn σ S S ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, k (σ x) = k x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, w (σ x) = b ↔ w x = a)

/-- Symmetric cells have the same size. -/
lemma cell_card_eq (h : LabelTransitive S w k) {a b : α} (ha : a ∈ S.image w)
    (hb : b ∈ S.image w) (c : β) :
    (fiber S (pairObs w k) (a, c)).card = (fiber S (pairObs w k) (b, c)).card := by
  obtain ⟨σ, hbij, hk, hw⟩ := h a ha b hb
  refine Finset.card_nbij σ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro x hx
    have hx' := Finset.mem_filter.mp hx
    simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq] at hx'
    refine Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hbij.mapsTo hx'.1, ?_⟩
    simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq]
    exact ⟨(hw x hx'.1).mpr hx'.2.1, by rw [hk x hx'.1, hx'.2.2]⟩
  · intro x hx y hy hxy
    exact hbij.injOn (fiber_subset (Finset.mem_coe.mp hx))
      (fiber_subset (Finset.mem_coe.mp hy)) hxy
  · intro y hy
    simp only [fiber, pairObs, coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Prod.mk.injEq] at hy
    obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := hbij.surjOn hy.1
    refine ⟨x, ?_, rfl⟩
    simp only [fiber, pairObs, coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Prod.mk.injEq]
    exact ⟨hx, (hw x hx).mp hy.2.1, by rw [← hk x hx, hy.2.2]⟩

/-- In each readout cell the label is uniform. -/
lemma prob_cell_eq (h : LabelTransitive S w k) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ S.image w) (c : β) :
    prob S (pairObs w k) (a, c) * (S.image w).card = prob S k c := by
  rw [← sum_prob_pair_left (S := S) (f := w) (g := k) c]
  have : ∀ b ∈ S.image w, prob S (pairObs w k) (b, c) = prob S (pairObs w k) (a, c) := by
    intro b hb
    unfold prob
    rw [cell_card_eq h hb ha c]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl this, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm]

/-- The label itself is uniform. -/
lemma prob_label_eq (h : LabelTransitive S w k) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ S.image w) :
    prob S w a * (S.image w).card = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx, _⟩ := mem_image.mp ha
  rw [← sum_prob_pair_right (S := S) (f := w) (g := k) a, Finset.sum_mul,
    Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun c _ => prob_cell_eq h ha c), sum_prob ⟨x, hx⟩]

/-- **The symmetry wall.**  If the readout-preserving symmetries act transitively on the
label values, the readout carries *exactly* zero bits about the label, while the label
carries *exactly* `log₂ #labels` bits. -/
theorem symmetry_wall (h : LabelTransitive S w k) :
    mutualInfo S w k = 0 ∧ entropy S w = logb 2 (S.image w).card := by
  constructor
  · refine mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_prob_mul (fun a ha c _ => ?_)
    have h1 := prob_cell_eq h ha c
    have h2 := prob_label_eq h ha
    have hm : ((S.image w).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr ⟨a, ha⟩).ne'
    have hpa : prob S w a = 1 / (S.image w).card := by
      field_simp; linarith
    rw [hpa]
    field_simp
    linarith
  · rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hS | hS
    · subst hS; simp [entropy]
    obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := hS
    refine entropy_eq_logb_card_of_uniform_fibers (k := (fiber S w (w x₀)).card) ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩
      (card_pos.mpr ⟨x₀, mem_filter.mpr ⟨hx₀, rfl⟩⟩) (fun a ha => ?_)
    have h1 := prob_label_eq h ha
    have h2 := prob_label_eq h (mem_image_of_mem w hx₀)
    have hm : ((S.image w).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr ⟨a, ha⟩).ne'
    have hS : (S.card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩).ne'
    have : prob S w a = prob S w (w x₀) := by
      have := h1.trans h2.symm
      exact mul_right_cancel₀ hm this
    unfold prob at this
    rw [div_left_inj' hS] at this
    exact_mod_cast this

end Abstract

/-! ## 2. The Galois semiprime wall -/

section Semiprime

variable {G : Type*} {τ : Type*} [LinearOrder τ]

/-- A readout of the Galois group that is constant on conjugacy classes (within `S`). -/
def IsClassFn [Group G] {κ : Type*} (S : Finset G) (H : G → κ) : Prop :=
  ∀ g ∈ S, ∀ h ∈ S, H (g * h * g⁻¹) = H h

/-- **The residue of `N` is a class function.**  A coset readout of the derived subgroup
is constant on conjugacy classes, because `(g h g⁻¹) h⁻¹` is a commutator. -/
theorem cosetReadout_isClassFn [Group G] {κ : Type*} {S N : Finset G} {c : G → κ}
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hD : IsDerivedFinset S N) (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c) :
    IsClassFn S c := by
  intro g hg h hh
  have hmem : g * h * g⁻¹ ∈ S := hS.mul_mem _ (hS.mul_mem _ hg _ hh) _ (hS.inv_mem _ hg)
  exact (hc _ hmem h hh).mpr (hD.commutator_mem g hg h hh)

/-- **Class functions of `σ_p σ_q` are swap-invariant**: `σ_q σ_p = σ_p⁻¹ (σ_p σ_q) σ_p`. -/
theorem classFn_mul_swap [Group G] {κ : Type*} {S : Finset G} {H : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S)
    (hH : IsClassFn S H) {x y : G} (hx : x ∈ S) (hy : y ∈ S) :
    H (y * x) = H (x * y) := by
  have := hH x⁻¹ (hS.inv_mem _ hx) (x * y) (hS.mul_mem _ hx _ hy)
  rw [inv_inv] at this
  rw [← this]
  congr 1
  group

/-- The semiprime sample space: ordered pairs of candidate Frobenius elements whose
splitting types differ (so that "which factor?" is a genuine question). -/
def asymPairs (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) : Finset (G × G) :=
  (A ×ˢ A).filter (fun z => T z.1 ≠ T z.2)

/-- The which-factor bit: does the first factor carry the smaller splitting type? -/
def whichBit (T : G → τ) (z : G × G) : Bool := decide (T z.1 < T z.2)

lemma swap_mem_asymPairs {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {z : G × G} (hz : z ∈ asymPairs A T) :
    z.swap ∈ asymPairs A T := by
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter, mem_product, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap] at hz ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨hz.1.2, hz.1.1⟩, fun h => hz.2 h.symm⟩

lemma whichBit_swap {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {z : G × G} (hz : z ∈ asymPairs A T) :
    whichBit T z.swap = !whichBit T z := by
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter] at hz
  simp only [whichBit, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hz.2 with h | h
  · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h.le]
  · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h.le]

/-- Swap-invariant readouts make the which-factor bit label-transitive. -/
lemma whichBit_labelTransitive {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ)
    (k : G × G → κ) (hk : ∀ z ∈ asymPairs A T, k z.swap = k z) :
    LabelTransitive (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) k := by
  intro a _ b _
  by_cases hab : a = b
  · subst hab
    exact ⟨id, Set.bijOn_id _, fun _ _ => rfl, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  · have hb : b = !a := by cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all
    refine ⟨Prod.swap, ⟨fun z hz => swap_mem_asymPairs hz, fun x _ y _ hxy => by
      simpa using congrArg Prod.swap hxy, fun z hz => ⟨z.swap, swap_mem_asymPairs hz,
        Prod.swap_swap z⟩⟩, hk, fun z hz => ?_⟩
    rw [whichBit_swap hz, hb]
    cases whichBit T z <;> cases a <;> simp

/-- **The Galois which-factor wall.**  Over an arbitrary finite Galois group (abelian or
not), for *every* readout `k` of the semiprime that is invariant under exchanging the two
factors, `k` carries *exactly* zero bits about which factor carries the smaller splitting
type — and that bit is a genuine full bit whenever the sample space is nonempty. -/
theorem galois_whichFactor_wall {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ)
    (k : G × G → κ) (hk : ∀ z ∈ asymPairs A T, k z.swap = k z) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) k = 0 ∧
      ((asymPairs A T).Nonempty → entropy (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) = 1) := by
  obtain ⟨h0, hH⟩ := symmetry_wall (whichBit_labelTransitive A T k hk)
  refine ⟨h0, fun ⟨z, hz⟩ => ?_⟩
  rw [hH]
  have himg : (asymPairs A T).image (whichBit T) = {true, false} := by
    apply Finset.Subset.antisymm
    · intro b _; cases b <;> simp
    · intro b hb
      have hz' := swap_mem_asymPairs hz
      have hw := whichBit_swap hz
      rcases (show b = whichBit T z ∨ b = whichBit T z.swap by
          rw [hw]; simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hb
          cases b <;> cases whichBit T z <;> simp_all) with rfl | rfl
      · exact mem_image_of_mem _ hz
      · exact mem_image_of_mem _ hz'
  rw [himg]
  simp

/-- **Residue and unordered types hide the which-factor bit.**  Let `S` be a finite Galois
group with derived subgroup `N`, `c` the residue (coset) readout, and `T` the splitting
type.  The readout an arithmetic adversary actually has on `N = p q` — the residue class
of `N` (coset of `σ_p σ_q`) *together with* the unordered pair of splitting types —
carries exactly zero bits about which factor carries which type. -/
theorem residue_and_types_hide_whichFactor [Group G] {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] {S N : Finset G}
    {c : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hD : IsDerivedFinset S N)
    (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs S T) (whichBit T)
        (fun z => (c (z.1 * z.2), min (T z.1) (T z.2), max (T z.1) (T z.2))) = 0 := by
  refine (galois_whichFactor_wall S T _ (fun z hz => ?_)).1
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter, mem_product] at hz
  simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, min_comm, max_comm]
  rw [classFn_mul_swap hS (cosetReadout_isClassFn hS hD hc) hz.1.1 hz.1.2]

/-- The same wall for the *conjugacy class* (Artin symbol) of `σ_p σ_q`: any class
function of the product, together with the unordered types, hides the bit. -/
theorem artin_and_types_hide_whichFactor [Group G] {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] {S : Finset G}
    {H : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hH : IsClassFn S H) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs S T) (whichBit T)
        (fun z => (H (z.1 * z.2), min (T z.1) (T z.2), max (T z.1) (T z.2))) = 0 := by
  refine (galois_whichFactor_wall S T _ (fun z hz => ?_)).1
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter, mem_product] at hz
  simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, min_comm, max_comm]
  rw [classFn_mul_swap hS hH hz.1.1 hz.1.2]

/-- **Non-vacuity.**  The *ordered* type readout recovers the full which-factor entropy. -/
theorem galois_whichFactor_ordered_full (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) (fun z => (T z.1, T z.2))
      = entropy (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) :=
  mutualInfo_eq_left_of_factors (φ := fun u : τ × τ => decide (u.1 < u.2)) (fun _ _ => rfl)

end Semiprime

/-! ## 3. The multi-prime wall -/

section MultiPrime

variable {G : Type*} {τ : Type*} [LinearOrder τ]

/-- The sample space for `N = p₀ ⋯ p_m`: tuples of candidate Frobenius elements in `A`
whose splitting types are pairwise distinct. -/
def distinctTuples (m : ℕ) (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) : Finset (Fin (m + 1) → G) :=
  (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ => A)).filter (fun x => Function.Injective (fun i => T (x i)))

/-- The label: the set of factors carrying the smallest splitting type (a singleton on
`distinctTuples`). -/
def minFactor {m : ℕ} (T : G → τ) (x : Fin (m + 1) → G) : Finset (Fin (m + 1)) :=
  univ.filter (fun i => ∀ j, T (x i) ≤ T (x j))

lemma minFactor_comp_perm {m : ℕ} (T : G → τ) (x : Fin (m + 1) → G)
    (s : Equiv.Perm (Fin (m + 1))) :
    minFactor T (x ∘ s) = (minFactor T x).image s.symm := by
  ext l
  simp only [minFactor, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Function.comp, mem_image]
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨s l, fun j => ?_, by simp⟩
    simpa using h (s.symm j)
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ j
    simpa using hi (s j)

lemma minFactor_singleton {m : ℕ} {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {x : Fin (m + 1) → G}
    (hx : x ∈ distinctTuples m A T) : ∃ i, minFactor T x = {i} := by
  simp only [distinctTuples, mem_filter] at hx
  obtain ⟨i, -, hi⟩ := Finset.exists_min_image univ (fun i => T (x i)) univ_nonempty
  refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
  ext l
  simp only [minFactor, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, mem_singleton]
  constructor
  · intro hl
    exact hx.2 (le_antisymm (hl i) (hi l (mem_univ _)))
  · rintro rfl j; exact hi j (mem_univ _)

lemma comp_swap_mem {m : ℕ} {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {x : Fin (m + 1) → G}
    (hx : x ∈ distinctTuples m A T) (i j : Fin (m + 1)) :
    x ∘ Equiv.swap i j ∈ distinctTuples m A T := by
  simp only [distinctTuples, mem_filter, Fintype.mem_piFinset, Function.comp] at hx ⊢
  exact ⟨fun t => hx.1 _, fun a b hab => (Equiv.swap i j).injective (hx.2 hab)⟩

/-- Transposition-invariant readouts make the min-factor label transitive. -/
lemma minFactor_labelTransitive {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (m : ℕ) (A : Finset G)
    (T : G → τ) (k : (Fin (m + 1) → G) → κ)
    (hk : ∀ x ∈ distinctTuples m A T, ∀ i j, k (x ∘ Equiv.swap i j) = k x) :
    LabelTransitive (distinctTuples m A T) (minFactor T) k := by
  intro a ha b hb
  obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := mem_image.mp ha
  obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := mem_image.mp hb
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := minFactor_singleton hx
  obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := minFactor_singleton hy
  rw [hi, hj]
  refine ⟨fun z => z ∘ Equiv.swap i j, ⟨fun z hz => comp_swap_mem hz i j, ?_, ?_⟩,
    fun z hz => hk z hz i j, fun z _ => ?_⟩
  · intro u _ v _ huv
    funext t
    have := congrFun huv (Equiv.swap i j t)
    simpa using this
  · intro z hz
    exact ⟨z ∘ Equiv.swap i j, comp_swap_mem hz i j, by
      ext t; simp [Function.comp]⟩
  · rw [minFactor_comp_perm, Equiv.symm_swap]
    constructor
    · intro h
      have := congrArg (Finset.image (Equiv.swap i j)) h
      simpa [Finset.image_image, Function.comp_def] using this
    · intro h
      rw [h]; simp

/-- **The multi-prime which-factor wall.**  For `N = p₀ ⋯ p_m` with pairwise distinct
splitting types (Frobenius candidates in any finite set `A` of any group), *which factor
carries the smallest splitting type* is a label of exactly `log₂ (m + 1)` bits, and every
readout of the tuple that is invariant under exchanging two factors — the residue of `N`
in an abelian quotient, the multiset of splitting types, any symmetric function of the
factors — carries **exactly zero** bits about it. -/
theorem multiFactor_wall {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (m : ℕ) (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ)
    (k : (Fin (m + 1) → G) → κ)
    (hk : ∀ x ∈ distinctTuples m A T, ∀ i j, k (x ∘ Equiv.swap i j) = k x) :
    mutualInfo (distinctTuples m A T) (minFactor T) k = 0 ∧
      ((distinctTuples m A T).Nonempty →
        entropy (distinctTuples m A T) (minFactor T) = logb 2 (m + 1)) := by
  obtain ⟨h0, hH⟩ := symmetry_wall (minFactor_labelTransitive m A T k hk)
  refine ⟨h0, fun ⟨x, hx⟩ => ?_⟩
  rw [hH]
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := minFactor_singleton hx
  have himg : (distinctTuples m A T).image (minFactor T) = univ.image (fun j => {j}) := by
    ext a
    simp only [mem_image, mem_univ, true_and]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
      obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := minFactor_singleton hy
      exact ⟨j, hj.symm⟩
    · rintro ⟨j, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨x ∘ Equiv.swap i j, comp_swap_mem hx i j, ?_⟩
      rw [minFactor_comp_perm, hi, Equiv.symm_swap]
      simp
  rw [himg, Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun a b h => Finset.singleton_injective h),
    card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
  push_cast
  ring_nf

/-- **Non-vacuity.**  The ordered tuple of splitting types determines the label, so the
ordered readout carries its full entropy. -/
theorem multiFactor_ordered_full (m : ℕ) (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (distinctTuples m A T) (minFactor T) (fun x i => T (x i))
      = entropy (distinctTuples m A T) (minFactor T) :=
  mutualInfo_eq_left_of_factors
    (φ := fun t : Fin (m + 1) → τ => univ.filter (fun i => ∀ j, t i ≤ t j)) (fun _ _ => rfl)

end MultiPrime

  exact mutualInfo_le_left _ _ _

/-- **Pure synergy: the residue of `N` is blind to each factor separately.**  For any
readout `F` of a single Frobenius element (its splitting type, its residue class, its
conjugacy class, …), the residue of `N = p q` carries exactly zero bits about `F(σ_p)`
and exactly zero bits about `F(σ_q)`. -/
theorem semiprime_residue_blind_to_each_factor {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hD : IsDerivedFinset S N) (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c)
    (F : G → α) :
    mutualInfo (S ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => c (z.1 * z.2)) (fun z => F z.1) = 0 ∧
      mutualInfo (S ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => c (z.1 * z.2)) (fun z => F z.2) = 0 := by
  have h1 : mutualInfo (S ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => c (z.1 * z.2)) (fun z => F z.1) = 0 := by
    rw [mutualInfo_comm]
    exact frobenius_one_time_pad hS (subset_refl S) F c
  refine ⟨h1, ?_⟩
  have himg : (S ×ˢ S).image Prod.swap = S ×ˢ S := by
    ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [mem_image, mem_product, Prod.exists, Prod.swap_prod_mk, Prod.mk.injEq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl, rfl⟩; exact ⟨hb, ha⟩
    · rintro ⟨hx, hy⟩; exact ⟨y, x, ⟨hy, hx⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
  have hinj : Set.InjOn (Prod.swap : G × G → G × G) (S ×ˢ S : Finset (G × G)) :=
    fun a _ b _ h => Prod.swap_injective h
  rw [← himg, mutualInfo_image_of_injOn hinj]
  rw [← h1]
  refine mutualInfo_congr (fun z hz => ?_) (fun _ _ => rfl)
  simp only [mem_product] at hz
  simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
  exact classFn_mul_swap hS (cosetReadout_isClassFn hS hD hc) hz.1 hz.2

/-- **`S₄`: pure synergy in a five-type field.**  The residue (sign coset) of `N = p q`
carries zero bits about the splitting type of `p`, zero bits about that of `q`, exactly
one bit about the unordered pair of types, and never more than one bit about anything. -/
theorem S4_semiprime_pure_synergy :
    mutualInfo (S4 ×ˢ S4) (prodCoset signIdx) (fun z => splitType z.1) = 0 ∧
    mutualInfo (S4 ×ˢ S4) (prodCoset signIdx) (fun z => splitType z.2) = 0 ∧
    mutualInfo (S4 ×ˢ S4) (prodCoset signIdx) symType = 1 ∧
    (∀ (R : Equiv.Perm (Fin 4) × Equiv.Perm (Fin 4) → ℕ × ℕ),
      mutualInfo (S4 ×ˢ S4) (prodCoset signIdx) R ≤ 1) := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := semiprime_residue_blind_to_each_factor S4_isSubgroup S4_derived S4_coset
    splitType
  refine ⟨h1, h2, S4_semi_channel, fun R => ?_⟩
  have hcap := semiprime_residue_cap S4_isSubgroup A4_isSubgroup S4_derived.subset S4_coset R
  have himg : (S4.image signIdx).card = 2 := by decide
  rw [himg] at hcap
  simpa using hcap

/-- **`D₄`: pure synergy above the binary ceiling.**  The residue of `N = p q` in the `D₄`
field is blind to each factor's splitting type, yet carries more than one bit about the
unordered pair — and at most `2 = log₂ [D₄ : C₂]` bits about anything. -/
theorem D4_semiprime_pure_synergy :
    mutualInfo (D4 ×ˢ D4) (prodCoset d4Idx) (fun z => splitType z.1) = 0 ∧
    mutualInfo (D4 ×ˢ D4) (prodCoset d4Idx) (fun z => splitType z.2) = 0 ∧
    1 < mutualInfo (D4 ×ˢ D4) (prodCoset d4Idx) symType ∧
    (∀ (R : Equiv.Perm (Fin 4) × Equiv.Perm (Fin 4) → ℕ × ℕ),
      mutualInfo (D4 ×ˢ D4) (prodCoset d4Idx) R ≤ 2) := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := semiprime_residue_blind_to_each_factor D4_isSubgroup D4_derived D4_coset
    splitType
  refine ⟨h1, h2, ?_, fun R => ?_⟩
  · rw [D4_semi_channel]
    have h3 := logb2_three_lt_two
    have h5 := logb2_five_gt_two
    linarith
  · have hcap := semiprime_residue_cap D4_isSubgroup Z4c_isSubgroup D4_derived.subset
      D4_coset R
    have himg : (D4.image d4Idx).card = 4 := by decide
    rw [himg] at hcap
    have : logb 2 (4 : ℝ) = 2 := by
      rw [show (4 : ℝ) = 2 ^ (2 : ℕ) by norm_num, Real.logb_pow]
      simp
    simpa [this] using hcap

/-! ## The semiprime which-factor wall for every group and every type readout

The catalog checks `I(coset(σ_p σ_q) ; ordered types) = I(coset(σ_p σ_q) ; unordered types)`
numerically for six fields (`S3_which_factor_wall`, …, `C4_which_factor_wall`).  We prove
it for *every* sample space closed under exchanging the factors, *every* swap-invariant
readout (in particular every class function of `σ_p σ_q`, e.g. the residue of `N`), and
*every* splitting-type readout `T`. -/

section OrderedWall

variable {τ : Type*} [LinearOrder τ] [DecidableEq τ]

/-- The unordered pair of splitting types. -/
def symPair (T : G → τ) (z : G × G) : τ × τ := (min (T z.1) (T z.2), max (T z.1) (T z.2))

/-- The ordered pair of splitting types. -/
def ordPair (T : G → τ) (z : G × G) : τ × τ := (T z.1, T z.2)

omit [Group G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq τ] in
/-- The ordered pair is the unordered pair plus the which-factor bit. -/
lemma ordPair_eq_reconstruct (T : G → τ) (z : G × G) :
    ordPair T z = (if whichBit T z then symPair T z else ((symPair T z).2, (symPair T z).1)) := by
  unfold ordPair symPair whichBit
  rcases lt_trichotomy (T z.1) (T z.2) with h | h | h
  · simp [h, min_eq_left h.le, max_eq_right h.le]
  · simp [h]
  · simp [not_lt.mpr h.le, min_eq_right h.le, max_eq_left h.le]

omit [Group G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq τ] in
lemma symPair_swap (T : G → τ) (z : G × G) : symPair T z.swap = symPair T z := by
  simp [symPair, min_comm, max_comm]

omit [Group G] [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq κ] in
/-- On a fibre of the unordered type pair, exchanging the factors is label-transitive for
the which-factor bit. -/
lemma whichBit_labelTransitive_fiber {Ω₀ : Finset (G × G)} (hΩ : ∀ z ∈ Ω₀, z.swap ∈ Ω₀)
    (k : G × G → κ) (hk : ∀ z ∈ Ω₀, k z.swap = k z) (T : G → τ) (s : τ × τ) :
    LabelTransitive (fiber Ω₀ (symPair T) s) (whichBit T) k := by
  intro a ha b hb
  by_cases hab : a = b
  · subst hab
    exact ⟨id, Set.bijOn_id _, fun _ _ => rfl, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  have hbna : b = !a := by cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all
  -- some element of the fibre has strictly ordered types, hence `s.1 < s.2`
  have hlt : s.1 < s.2 := by
    have htrue : true ∈ (fiber Ω₀ (symPair T) s).image (whichBit T) := by
      cases a
      · rw [hbna] at hb; exact hb
      · exact ha
    obtain ⟨z, hz, hzt⟩ := mem_image.mp htrue
    have hs := (mem_filter.mp hz).2
    simp only [whichBit, decide_eq_true_eq] at hzt
    rw [← hs]
    simp [symPair, min_eq_left hzt.le, max_eq_right hzt.le, hzt]
  have hne : ∀ x ∈ fiber Ω₀ (symPair T) s, T x.1 ≠ T x.2 := by
    intro x hx heq
    have hs := (mem_filter.mp hx).2
    rw [← hs] at hlt
    simp [symPair, heq] at hlt
  have hmem : ∀ x ∈ fiber Ω₀ (symPair T) s, x.swap ∈ fiber Ω₀ (symPair T) s := by
    intro x hx
    obtain ⟨hx1, hx2⟩ := mem_filter.mp hx
    exact mem_filter.mpr ⟨hΩ x hx1, by rw [symPair_swap]; exact hx2⟩
  refine ⟨Prod.swap, ⟨hmem, fun x _ y _ hxy => Prod.swap_injective hxy,
    fun z hz => ⟨z.swap, hmem z hz, Prod.swap_swap z⟩⟩,
    fun x hx => hk x (mem_filter.mp hx).1, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  have hflip : whichBit T x.swap = !whichBit T x := by
    simp only [whichBit, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne (hne x hx) with h | h
    · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h.le]
    · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h.le]
  rw [hflip, hbna]
  cases whichBit T x <;> cases a <;> simp

omit [Group G] [DecidableEq G] in
/-- **The semiprime which-factor wall, in general.**  On any sample space of ordered pairs
closed under exchanging the factors, for any readout `k` invariant under the exchange and
any splitting-type readout `T`, the ordered type pair carries *exactly* the same
information about `k` as the unordered one. -/
theorem ordered_eq_unordered_of_swap_invariant {Ω₀ : Finset (G × G)}
    (hΩ : ∀ z ∈ Ω₀, z.swap ∈ Ω₀) (k : G × G → κ) (hk : ∀ z ∈ Ω₀, k z.swap = k z)
    (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo Ω₀ k (ordPair T) = mutualInfo Ω₀ k (symPair T) := by
  -- the ordered pair induces the same partition as (unordered pair, which-factor bit)
  have hpart : mutualInfo Ω₀ k (ordPair T) = mutualInfo Ω₀ k (pairObs (symPair T) (whichBit T)) := by
    rw [mutualInfo_comm Ω₀ k, mutualInfo_comm Ω₀ k]
    refine mutualInfo_congr_partition k (fun z _ z' _ => ?_)
    simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      rw [ordPair_eq_reconstruct T z, ordPair_eq_reconstruct T z', h1, h2]
    · intro h
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · simp only [symPair]
        simp only [ordPair, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
        rw [h.1, h.2]
      · simp only [whichBit]
        simp only [ordPair, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
        rw [h.1, h.2]
  rw [hpart, mutualInfo_pair_chain]
  have hcond : condMutualInfo Ω₀ k (whichBit T) (symPair T) = 0 := by
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun s _ => ?_)
    rw [mutualInfo_comm,
      (symmetry_wall (whichBit_labelTransitive_fiber hΩ k hk T s)).1, mul_zero]
  rw [hcond, add_zero]

omit [DecidableEq G] in
/-- **Corollary: the residue of `N` never learns which factor is which.**  For every
finite Galois group `S`, every class function `H` (residue class of `N`, Artin symbol,
cycle type of `σ_p σ_q`, …) and every splitting-type readout `T`,
`I(H(σ_p σ_q) ; (T p, T q)) = I(H(σ_p σ_q) ; {T p, T q})`.  This proves the catalog's six
numerical which-factor walls (`S3_which_factor_wall`, …) in full generality. -/
theorem semiprime_whichFactor_wall_general {H : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S)
    (hH : IsClassFn S H) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (S ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) (ordPair T)
      = mutualInfo (S ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) (symPair T) := by
  refine ordered_eq_unordered_of_swap_invariant (fun z hz => ?_) _ (fun z hz => ?_) T
  · simp only [mem_product] at hz ⊢
    exact ⟨hz.2, hz.1⟩
  · simp only [mem_product] at hz
    simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
    exact classFn_mul_swap hS hH hz.1 hz.2

/-- The catalog's numerically verified which-factor walls for `S₄` and `D₄`, re-derived
from the general theorem without evaluating a single entropy. -/
theorem S4_D4_which_factor_walls_structural :
    mutualInfo (S4 ×ˢ S4) (prodCoset signIdx) ordType
        = mutualInfo (S4 ×ˢ S4) (prodCoset signIdx) symType ∧
    mutualInfo (D4 ×ˢ D4) (prodCoset d4Idx) ordType
        = mutualInfo (D4 ×ˢ D4) (prodCoset d4Idx) symType :=
  ⟨semiprime_whichFactor_wall_general S4_isSubgroup
      (cosetReadout_isClassFn S4_isSubgroup S4_derived S4_coset) typeCode,
    semiprime_whichFactor_wall_general D4_isSubgroup
      (cosetReadout_isClassFn D4_isSubgroup D4_derived D4_coset) typeCode⟩

end OrderedWall

end GaloisSideChannel

end TypeChannel

import Cryptography.TypeChannelMilestone.InfoCalculus

/-!
# The Galois/Frobenius side channel: data processing and the independence law

This file strengthens two of the three closures of the Galois/Frobenius side-channel
family (`Cryptography.NonabelianTypeChannel.*`, the which-factor wall and the
Artin/torsor channel) from *support / one-readout* statements to *distributional,
all-post-processings* statements, in the finite Shannon calculus of
`Cryptography.NonabelianTypeChannel.Entropy`.

## Main results

* `mutualInfo_comp_left_le`, `mutualInfo_comp_both_le` — **data processing**:
  post-processing either readout never increases a channel.
* `residue_postprocess_le_index` — the **abelianization cap for every post-processed
  residue readout**: `I(ψ ∘ coset ; φ ∘ T) ≤ I(coset ; T) ≤ log₂ [S : N]`.  The catalog
  cap `typeChannel_le_logb_index` only covered the coset readout itself and injective
  relabellings of it (`residue_channel_eq_coset_channel`).
* `mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_card_mul` — the **independence law** in counting form: if every
  joint cell count factors, the channel is exactly zero.
* `frobenius_one_time_pad` — **the Artin channel is a one-time pad**: in *any* finite
  Galois group `S` (abelian or not), for any candidate set `A ⊆ S` of Frobenius elements
  of `p` and a Chebotarev-uniform Frobenius of `q` in `S`, *every* readout of the
  product `σ_p σ_q` carries
  **exactly zero** bits about *every* readout of `σ_p`.
* `frobenius_posterior_eq_prior` — the same, as "posterior = prior": conditioning on any
  observed value of the product readout leaves the law of every readout of `σ_p`
  unchanged.  This is the distributional strengthening of `nonabelian_no_pruning`
  (which only says the posterior has full *support*).
* `frobenius_pad_breaks_with_cofactor` — non-vacuity: once the Frobenius of the cofactor
  is also revealed, the product readout carries the full `log₂ |A|` bits.
-/

namespace TypeChannel

namespace GaloisSideChannel

open Finset Real

variable {Ω α β γ δ : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [DecidableEq δ]

/-! ## 1. Data processing -/

/-- **Data processing (left).**  Post-processing the first readout by any function `ψ`
never increases the channel: `I(ψ ∘ f ; g) ≤ I(f ; g)`. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comp_left_le (S : Finset Ω) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) (ψ : α → γ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun w => ψ (f w)) g ≤ mutualInfo S f g := by
  rw [mutualInfo_comm S _ g, mutualInfo_comm S f g]
  calc mutualInfo S g (fun w => ψ (f w))
      ≤ mutualInfo S g (pairObs (fun w => ψ (f w)) f) := mutualInfo_le_pair g _ f
    _ = mutualInfo S g f := by
        rw [mutualInfo_comm S g, mutualInfo_comm S g f]
        refine mutualInfo_congr_partition (c := f) (c' := pairObs (fun w => ψ (f w)) f) g ?_
        intro a _ b _
        simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq]
        constructor
        · intro h; exact ⟨by rw [h], h⟩
        · exact fun h => h.2

/-- **Data processing (right).** `I(f ; φ ∘ g) ≤ I(f ; g)`. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comp_right_le (S : Finset Ω) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) (φ : β → δ) :
    mutualInfo S f (fun w => φ (g w)) ≤ mutualInfo S f g := by
  rw [mutualInfo_comm S f _, mutualInfo_comm S f g]
  exact mutualInfo_comp_left_le S g f φ

/-- **Data processing (both sides).** `I(ψ ∘ f ; φ ∘ g) ≤ I(f ; g)`. -/
theorem mutualInfo_comp_both_le (S : Finset Ω) (f : Ω → α) (g : Ω → β) (ψ : α → γ)
    (φ : β → δ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun w => ψ (f w)) (fun w => φ (g w)) ≤ mutualInfo S f g :=
  (mutualInfo_comp_right_le S _ g φ).trans (mutualInfo_comp_left_le S f g ψ)

section Residue

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] {κ τ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] [DecidableEq τ]

/-- **The abelianization cap for every post-processed residue readout.**  Let `S` be a
finite Galois group, `N` its derived subgroup and `c` the coset (residue-class) readout.
For *any* coarsening `ψ` of the residue (e.g. reducing `p` to a smaller modulus, or
any arithmetic function of the residue) and *any* post-processing `φ` of the splitting
type, the channel is bounded by the coset channel, and hence by `log₂ [S : N]`. -/
theorem residue_postprocess_le_index {S N : Finset G} {c : G → κ}
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hN : IsSubgroupFinset N) (hNS : N ⊆ S)
    (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c) (T : G → τ) (ψ : κ → γ) (φ : τ → δ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun g => ψ (c g)) (fun g => φ (T g)) ≤ mutualInfo S c T ∧
      mutualInfo S c T ≤ logb 2 (S.image c).card :=
  ⟨mutualInfo_comp_both_le S c T ψ φ, typeChannel_le_logb_index hS hN hNS hc T⟩

omit [DecidableEq G] in
/-- In a perfect Galois group *every* post-processed residue readout leaks exactly
nothing about *every* post-processed type readout. -/
theorem residue_postprocess_eq_zero_of_perfect {S : Finset G} {c : G → κ}
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hc : IsCosetReadout S S c) (T : G → τ) (ψ : κ → γ)
    (φ : τ → δ) :
    mutualInfo S (fun g => ψ (c g)) (fun g => φ (T g)) = 0 := by
  have h1 := mutualInfo_comp_both_le S c T ψ φ
  rw [typeChannel_eq_zero_of_perfect hS hc T] at h1
  have h2 := mutualInfo_nonneg (S := S) ⟨1, hS.one_mem⟩ (fun g => ψ (c g)) (fun g => φ (T g))
  linarith

end Residue

/-! ## 2. The independence law -/

/-- **The independence law (probability form).**  If the joint law of `(f, g)` is the
product of the marginals on the product of the images, the channel is exactly zero. -/
theorem mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_prob_mul {S : Finset Ω} {f : Ω → α} {g : Ω → β}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ S.image f, ∀ b ∈ S.image g,
      prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b) = prob S f a * prob S g b) :
    mutualInfo S f g = 0 := by
  rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hS | hS
  · subst hS; simp [mutualInfo, entropy]
  have hpair : entropy S (pairObs f g) = entropy S f + entropy S g := by
    rw [entropy_eq_sum_of_subset (image_pairObs_subset (S := S) (f := f) (g := g)),
      Finset.sum_product]
    have hterm : ∀ a ∈ S.image f, ∑ b ∈ S.image g,
        -(prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b) * logb 2 (prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b)))
          = -(prob S f a * logb 2 (prob S f a)) * ∑ b ∈ S.image g, prob S g b
            + prob S f a * ∑ b ∈ S.image g, -(prob S g b * logb 2 (prob S g b)) := by
      intro a ha
      rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun b hb => ?_)
      rw [h a ha b hb, Real.logb_mul (prob_pos_of_mem ha).ne' (prob_pos_of_mem hb).ne']
      ring
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_add_distrib, sum_prob hS]
    simp only [mul_one]
    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, sum_prob hS, one_mul]
    rfl
  unfold mutualInfo
  rw [hpair]; ring

/-- A joint cell count that factors gives a joint probability that factors. -/
lemma prob_pair_eq_mul_of_card_mul {S : Finset Ω} {f : Ω → α} {g : Ω → β} {a : α} {b : β}
    (hS : S.Nonempty)
    (h : (fiber S (pairObs f g) (a, b)).card * S.card = (fiber S f a).card * (fiber S g b).card) :
    prob S (pairObs f g) (a, b) = prob S f a * prob S g b := by
  have hS' : (S.card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr hS).ne'
  have hc : ((fiber S (pairObs f g) (a, b)).card : ℝ) * S.card
      = (fiber S f a).card * (fiber S g b).card := by exact_mod_cast h
  unfold prob
  field_simp
  linarith

/-- **The independence law (counting form).**  If every joint cell count satisfies
`#{f = a, g = b} · |S| = #{f = a} · #{g = b}`, the channel is exactly zero. -/
theorem mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_card_mul {S : Finset Ω} {f : Ω → α} {g : Ω → β}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ S.image f, ∀ b ∈ S.image g,
      (fiber S (pairObs f g) (a, b)).card * S.card = (fiber S f a).card * (fiber S g b).card) :
    mutualInfo S f g = 0 := by
  refine mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_prob_mul (fun a ha b hb => ?_)
  obtain ⟨w, hw, _⟩ := mem_image.mp ha
  exact prob_pair_eq_mul_of_card_mul ⟨w, hw⟩ (h a ha b hb)

/-! ## 3. The Artin channel is a one-time pad -/

section OneTimePad

variable {G : Type*} [Group G] [DecidableEq G] {S A : Finset G}

/-- The counting core of the one-time pad: inside a finite Galois group `S`, the shear
`(x, z) ↦ (x, x⁻¹ z)` identifies the cell `{F x = a, H (x y) = b}` of `A × S` with a
product of a cell of `F` on `A` and a cell of `H` on `S`. -/
lemma card_shear_filter (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (P Q : G → Prop)
    [DecidablePred P] [DecidablePred Q] :
    ((A ×ˢ S).filter (fun z => P z.1 ∧ Q (z.1 * z.2))).card
      = (A.filter P).card * (S.filter Q).card := by
  have hset : (A ×ˢ S).filter (fun z => P z.1 ∧ Q (z.1 * z.2))
      = ((A.filter P) ×ˢ (S.filter Q)).image (fun u : G × G => (u.1, u.1⁻¹ * u.2)) := by
    ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [mem_filter, mem_product, mem_image, Prod.mk.injEq, Prod.exists]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨hx, hy⟩, hP, hQ⟩
      exact ⟨x, x * y, ⟨⟨hx, hP⟩, hS.mul_mem _ (hA hx) _ hy, hQ⟩, rfl, by group⟩
    · rintro ⟨u, v, ⟨⟨hu, hP⟩, hv, hQ⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
      refine ⟨⟨hu, hS.mul_mem _ (hS.inv_mem _ (hA hu)) _ hv⟩, hP, ?_⟩
      simpa using hQ
  rw [hset, Finset.card_image_of_injective, Finset.card_product]
  intro u v huv
  simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at huv
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := huv
  refine Prod.ext h1 ?_
  rw [h1] at h2
  exact mul_left_cancel h2

/-- The cell counts of the product channel factor exactly:
`#{F x = a, H (x y) = b} · |A × S| = #{F x = a} · #{H (x y) = b}`. -/
lemma pad_card_mul (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (F : G → α) (H : G → β)
    (a : α) (b : β) :
    (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (pairObs (fun z : G × G => F z.1)
      (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2))) (a, b)).card * (A ×ˢ S).card
      = (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => F z.1) a).card *
        (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b).card := by
  have h1 : (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (pairObs (fun z : G × G => F z.1)
      (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2))) (a, b)).card
      = (A.filter (fun x => F x = a)).card * (S.filter (fun x => H x = b)).card := by
    rw [← card_shear_filter hS hA]
    unfold fiber pairObs
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq]
  have h2 : (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => F z.1) a).card
      = (A.filter (fun x => F x = a)).card * (S.filter (fun _ => True)).card := by
    rw [← card_shear_filter hS hA]
    unfold fiber
    simp only [and_true]
  have h3 : (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b).card
      = (A.filter (fun _ => True)).card * (S.filter (fun x => H x = b)).card := by
    rw [← card_shear_filter hS hA]
    unfold fiber
    simp only [true_and]
  rw [h1, h2, h3, Finset.card_product]
  simp only [filter_true]
  ring

/-- **The Artin channel is a one-time pad.**  Let `S` be a finite (possibly non-abelian)
Galois group.  Model the Frobenius of `p` as uniform on an arbitrary candidate set
`A ⊆ S` and the Frobenius of `q` as uniform on `S` (Chebotarev).  Then *any* readout `H`
of the Frobenius of `N`, `σ_N = σ_p σ_q` — its conjugacy class, its abelianization coset,
its cycle type, anything — carries **exactly zero** bits about *any* readout `F` of
`σ_p`. -/
theorem frobenius_one_time_pad (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (F : G → α)
    (H : G → β) :
    mutualInfo (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => F z.1) (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2)) = 0 :=
  mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_card_mul (fun a _ b _ => pad_card_mul hS hA F H a b)

/-- **Posterior equals prior.**  For every observed value `b` of the readout of the
Frobenius of `N`, the conditional law of every readout of the Frobenius of `p` equals its
prior law.  `nonabelian_no_pruning` is the support shadow of this statement. -/
theorem frobenius_posterior_eq_prior (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S) (F : G → α)
    (H : G → β) (a : α) {b : β} (hb : b ∈ (A ×ˢ S).image (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2))) :
    prob (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => H (z.1 * z.2)) b) (fun z => F z.1) a
      = prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => F z.1) a := by
  have hpb : 0 < prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b := prob_pos_of_mem hb
  obtain ⟨w, hw, _⟩ := mem_image.mp hb
  have hjoint := prob_pair_eq_mul_of_card_mul ⟨w, hw⟩ (pad_card_mul hS hA F H a b)
  have hchain := prob_pair_eq_mul (S := A ×ˢ S) (X := fun z : G × G => F z.1)
    (t := fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) (a := a) hb
  rw [hjoint] at hchain
  have key : prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b *
      (prob (fiber (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => H (z.1 * z.2)) b) (fun z => F z.1) a
        - prob (A ×ˢ S) (fun z : G × G => F z.1) a) = 0 := by
    rw [mul_sub]; linarith
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp key with h | h
  · exact absurd h hpb.ne'
  · linarith

/-- **Non-vacuity: the pad breaks once the cofactor's Frobenius is revealed.**  The pair
(Frobenius of `N`, Frobenius of `q`) determines the Frobenius of `p`, so it carries the
full `log₂ |A|` bits about it.  The zero of `frobenius_one_time_pad` is therefore a
genuine independence phenomenon, not an entropy deficit. -/
theorem frobenius_pad_breaks_with_cofactor (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hA : A ⊆ S)
    (hA0 : A.Nonempty) :
    mutualInfo (A ×ˢ S) (fun z => z.1) (fun z => (z.1 * z.2, z.2)) = logb 2 A.card := by
  rw [mutualInfo_eq_left_of_factors (φ := fun u : G × G => u.1 * u.2⁻¹)
    (fun w _ => by simp)]
  have himg : (A ×ˢ S).image (fun z : G × G => z.1) = A := by
    ext x
    simp only [mem_image, mem_product, Prod.exists, exists_and_right, exists_eq_right]
    exact ⟨fun ⟨_, h, _⟩ => h, fun h => ⟨1, h, hS.one_mem⟩⟩
  rw [entropy_eq_logb_card_of_uniform_fibers (k := S.card)
    (hA0.product ⟨1, hS.one_mem⟩) (card_pos.mpr ⟨1, hS.one_mem⟩), himg]
  intro x hx
  rw [himg] at hx
  have := card_shear_filter hS hA (fun y => y = x) (fun _ => True)
  simp only [and_true, filter_true] at this
  unfold fiber
  rw [this, Finset.filter_eq' A x, if_pos hx, card_singleton, one_mul]

end OneTimePad

/-!
# The which-factor wall for Galois groups, for any number of prime factors

The catalog's which-factor wall (`CyclicTypeChannel.whichFactor_wall`,
`Combinatorics/D12SemiprimeWhichFactorWall.lean`) is stated for the cyclic exponent box
of `Q(ζ_ℓ)` and for a *binary* label.  This file lifts it to

* an **abstract symmetry wall** (`symmetry_wall`): whenever the readout-preserving
  symmetries of the sample space act transitively on the values of a label `w`, the
  label is *exactly* uniform (`log₂ #labels` bits) and *every* readout preserved by those
  symmetries carries *exactly* zero bits about it;
* the **Galois semiprime wall** (`galois_whichFactor_wall`) over an *arbitrary*, possibly
  non-abelian, finite Galois group, with the key arithmetic input proved rather than
  assumed: the residue class of `N = p q` (the abelianization coset of `σ_p σ_q`) and
  more generally every class function of `σ_p σ_q` is swap-invariant
  (`classFn_mul_swap`, `cosetReadout_isClassFn`), so the full readout
  (residue of `N`, unordered type pair) hides the which-factor bit completely
  (`residue_and_types_hide_whichFactor`);
* the **multi-prime wall** (`multiFactor_wall`): for `N = p₀ ⋯ p_m` with pairwise
  distinct splitting types, *which of the `m+1` factors carries the smallest type* is a
  label of exactly `log₂ (m+1)` bits, and every readout invariant under transposing two
  factors carries exactly zero bits about it.

Each wall is shown non-vacuous: the *ordered* readout recovers the whole label
(`galois_whichFactor_ordered_full`, `multiFactor_ordered_full`).
-/

namespace TypeChannel

namespace GaloisSideChannel

open Finset Real

variable {Ω α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]

/-! ## 1. The abstract symmetry wall -/

section Abstract

variable {S : Finset Ω} {w : Ω → α} {k : Ω → β}

/-- The hypothesis of the symmetry wall: for any two label values in use there is a
bijection of the sample space preserving the readout `k` and carrying the first label
class onto the second. -/
def LabelTransitive (S : Finset Ω) (w : Ω → α) (k : Ω → β) : Prop :=
  ∀ a ∈ S.image w, ∀ b ∈ S.image w, ∃ σ : Ω → Ω,
    Set.BijOn σ S S ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, k (σ x) = k x) ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, w (σ x) = b ↔ w x = a)

/-- Symmetric cells have the same size. -/
lemma cell_card_eq (h : LabelTransitive S w k) {a b : α} (ha : a ∈ S.image w)
    (hb : b ∈ S.image w) (c : β) :
    (fiber S (pairObs w k) (a, c)).card = (fiber S (pairObs w k) (b, c)).card := by
  obtain ⟨σ, hbij, hk, hw⟩ := h a ha b hb
  refine Finset.card_nbij σ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro x hx
    have hx' := Finset.mem_filter.mp hx
    simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq] at hx'
    refine Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hbij.mapsTo hx'.1, ?_⟩
    simp only [pairObs, Prod.mk.injEq]
    exact ⟨(hw x hx'.1).mpr hx'.2.1, by rw [hk x hx'.1, hx'.2.2]⟩
  · intro x hx y hy hxy
    exact hbij.injOn (fiber_subset (Finset.mem_coe.mp hx))
      (fiber_subset (Finset.mem_coe.mp hy)) hxy
  · intro y hy
    simp only [fiber, pairObs, coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Prod.mk.injEq] at hy
    obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := hbij.surjOn hy.1
    refine ⟨x, ?_, rfl⟩
    simp only [fiber, pairObs, coe_filter, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Prod.mk.injEq]
    exact ⟨hx, (hw x hx).mp hy.2.1, by rw [← hk x hx, hy.2.2]⟩

/-- In each readout cell the label is uniform. -/
lemma prob_cell_eq (h : LabelTransitive S w k) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ S.image w) (c : β) :
    prob S (pairObs w k) (a, c) * (S.image w).card = prob S k c := by
  rw [← sum_prob_pair_left (S := S) (f := w) (g := k) c]
  have : ∀ b ∈ S.image w, prob S (pairObs w k) (b, c) = prob S (pairObs w k) (a, c) := by
    intro b hb
    unfold prob
    rw [cell_card_eq h hb ha c]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl this, Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_comm]

/-- The label itself is uniform. -/
lemma prob_label_eq (h : LabelTransitive S w k) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ S.image w) :
    prob S w a * (S.image w).card = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx, _⟩ := mem_image.mp ha
  rw [← sum_prob_pair_right (S := S) (f := w) (g := k) a, Finset.sum_mul,
    Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun c _ => prob_cell_eq h ha c), sum_prob ⟨x, hx⟩]

/-- **The symmetry wall.**  If the readout-preserving symmetries act transitively on the
label values, the readout carries *exactly* zero bits about the label, while the label
carries *exactly* `log₂ #labels` bits. -/
theorem symmetry_wall (h : LabelTransitive S w k) :
    mutualInfo S w k = 0 ∧ entropy S w = logb 2 (S.image w).card := by
  constructor
  · refine mutualInfo_eq_zero_of_prob_mul (fun a ha c _ => ?_)
    have h1 := prob_cell_eq h ha c
    have h2 := prob_label_eq h ha
    have hm : ((S.image w).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr ⟨a, ha⟩).ne'
    have hpa : prob S w a = 1 / (S.image w).card := by
      field_simp; linarith
    rw [hpa]
    field_simp
    linarith
  · rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hS | hS
    · subst hS; simp [entropy]
    obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := hS
    refine entropy_eq_logb_card_of_uniform_fibers (k := (fiber S w (w x₀)).card) ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩
      (card_pos.mpr ⟨x₀, mem_filter.mpr ⟨hx₀, rfl⟩⟩) (fun a ha => ?_)
    have h1 := prob_label_eq h ha
    have h2 := prob_label_eq h (mem_image_of_mem w hx₀)
    have hm : ((S.image w).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
      exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr ⟨a, ha⟩).ne'
    have hS : (S.card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast (card_pos.mpr ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩).ne'
    have : prob S w a = prob S w (w x₀) := by
      have := h1.trans h2.symm
      exact mul_right_cancel₀ hm this
    unfold prob at this
    rw [div_left_inj' hS] at this
    exact_mod_cast this

end Abstract

/-! ## 2. The Galois semiprime wall -/

section Semiprime

variable {G : Type*} {τ : Type*} [LinearOrder τ]

/-- A readout of the Galois group that is constant on conjugacy classes (within `S`). -/
def IsClassFn [Group G] {κ : Type*} (S : Finset G) (H : G → κ) : Prop :=
  ∀ g ∈ S, ∀ h ∈ S, H (g * h * g⁻¹) = H h

/-- **The residue of `N` is a class function.**  A coset readout of the derived subgroup
is constant on conjugacy classes, because `(g h g⁻¹) h⁻¹` is a commutator. -/
theorem cosetReadout_isClassFn [Group G] {κ : Type*} {S N : Finset G} {c : G → κ}
    (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hD : IsDerivedFinset S N) (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c) :
    IsClassFn S c := by
  intro g hg h hh
  have hmem : g * h * g⁻¹ ∈ S := hS.mul_mem _ (hS.mul_mem _ hg _ hh) _ (hS.inv_mem _ hg)
  exact (hc _ hmem h hh).mpr (hD.commutator_mem g hg h hh)

/-- **Class functions of `σ_p σ_q` are swap-invariant**: `σ_q σ_p = σ_p⁻¹ (σ_p σ_q) σ_p`. -/
theorem classFn_mul_swap [Group G] {κ : Type*} {S : Finset G} {H : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S)
    (hH : IsClassFn S H) {x y : G} (hx : x ∈ S) (hy : y ∈ S) :
    H (y * x) = H (x * y) := by
  have := hH x⁻¹ (hS.inv_mem _ hx) (x * y) (hS.mul_mem _ hx _ hy)
  rw [inv_inv] at this
  rw [← this]
  congr 1
  group

/-- The semiprime sample space: ordered pairs of candidate Frobenius elements whose
splitting types differ (so that "which factor?" is a genuine question). -/
def asymPairs (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) : Finset (G × G) :=
  (A ×ˢ A).filter (fun z => T z.1 ≠ T z.2)

/-- The which-factor bit: does the first factor carry the smaller splitting type? -/
def whichBit (T : G → τ) (z : G × G) : Bool := decide (T z.1 < T z.2)

lemma swap_mem_asymPairs {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {z : G × G} (hz : z ∈ asymPairs A T) :
    z.swap ∈ asymPairs A T := by
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter, mem_product, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap] at hz ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨hz.1.2, hz.1.1⟩, fun h => hz.2 h.symm⟩

lemma whichBit_swap {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {z : G × G} (hz : z ∈ asymPairs A T) :
    whichBit T z.swap = !whichBit T z := by
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter] at hz
  simp only [whichBit, Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap]
  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hz.2 with h | h
  · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h.le]
  · simp [h, not_lt.mpr h.le]

/-- Swap-invariant readouts make the which-factor bit label-transitive. -/
lemma whichBit_labelTransitive {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ)
    (k : G × G → κ) (hk : ∀ z ∈ asymPairs A T, k z.swap = k z) :
    LabelTransitive (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) k := by
  intro a _ b _
  by_cases hab : a = b
  · subst hab
    exact ⟨id, Set.bijOn_id _, fun _ _ => rfl, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩
  · have hb : b = !a := by cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all
    refine ⟨Prod.swap, ⟨fun z hz => swap_mem_asymPairs hz, fun x _ y _ hxy => by
      simpa using congrArg Prod.swap hxy, fun z hz => ⟨z.swap, swap_mem_asymPairs hz,
        Prod.swap_swap z⟩⟩, hk, fun z hz => ?_⟩
    rw [whichBit_swap hz, hb]
    cases whichBit T z <;> cases a <;> simp

/-- **The Galois which-factor wall.**  Over an arbitrary finite Galois group (abelian or
not), for *every* readout `k` of the semiprime that is invariant under exchanging the two
factors, `k` carries *exactly* zero bits about which factor carries the smaller splitting
type — and that bit is a genuine full bit whenever the sample space is nonempty. -/
theorem galois_whichFactor_wall {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ)
    (k : G × G → κ) (hk : ∀ z ∈ asymPairs A T, k z.swap = k z) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) k = 0 ∧
      ((asymPairs A T).Nonempty → entropy (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) = 1) := by
  obtain ⟨h0, hH⟩ := symmetry_wall (whichBit_labelTransitive A T k hk)
  refine ⟨h0, fun ⟨z, hz⟩ => ?_⟩
  rw [hH]
  have himg : (asymPairs A T).image (whichBit T) = {true, false} := by
    apply Finset.Subset.antisymm
    · intro b _; cases b <;> simp
    · intro b hb
      have hz' := swap_mem_asymPairs hz
      have hw := whichBit_swap hz
      rcases (show b = whichBit T z ∨ b = whichBit T z.swap by
          rw [hw]; simp only [mem_insert, mem_singleton] at hb
          cases b <;> cases whichBit T z <;> simp_all) with rfl | rfl
      · exact mem_image_of_mem _ hz
      · exact mem_image_of_mem _ hz'
  rw [himg]
  simp

/-- **Residue and unordered types hide the which-factor bit.**  Let `S` be a finite Galois
group with derived subgroup `N`, `c` the residue (coset) readout, and `T` the splitting
type.  The readout an arithmetic adversary actually has on `N = p q` — the residue class
of `N` (coset of `σ_p σ_q`) *together with* the unordered pair of splitting types —
carries exactly zero bits about which factor carries which type. -/
theorem residue_and_types_hide_whichFactor [Group G] {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] {S N : Finset G}
    {c : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hD : IsDerivedFinset S N)
    (hc : IsCosetReadout S N c) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs S T) (whichBit T)
        (fun z => (c (z.1 * z.2), min (T z.1) (T z.2), max (T z.1) (T z.2))) = 0 := by
  refine (galois_whichFactor_wall S T _ (fun z hz => ?_)).1
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter, mem_product] at hz
  simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, min_comm, max_comm]
  rw [classFn_mul_swap hS (cosetReadout_isClassFn hS hD hc) hz.1.1 hz.1.2]

/-- The same wall for the *conjugacy class* (Artin symbol) of `σ_p σ_q`: any class
function of the product, together with the unordered types, hides the bit. -/
theorem artin_and_types_hide_whichFactor [Group G] {κ : Type*} [DecidableEq κ] {S : Finset G}
    {H : G → κ} (hS : IsSubgroupFinset S) (hH : IsClassFn S H) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs S T) (whichBit T)
        (fun z => (H (z.1 * z.2), min (T z.1) (T z.2), max (T z.1) (T z.2))) = 0 := by
  refine (galois_whichFactor_wall S T _ (fun z hz => ?_)).1
  simp only [asymPairs, mem_filter, mem_product] at hz
  simp only [Prod.fst_swap, Prod.snd_swap, min_comm, max_comm]
  rw [classFn_mul_swap hS hH hz.1.1 hz.1.2]

/-- **Non-vacuity.**  The *ordered* type readout recovers the full which-factor entropy. -/
theorem galois_whichFactor_ordered_full (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) :
    mutualInfo (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) (fun z => (T z.1, T z.2))
      = entropy (asymPairs A T) (whichBit T) :=
  mutualInfo_eq_left_of_factors (φ := fun u : τ × τ => decide (u.1 < u.2)) (fun _ _ => rfl)

end Semiprime

/-! ## 3. The multi-prime wall -/

section MultiPrime

variable {G : Type*} {τ : Type*} [LinearOrder τ]

/-- The sample space for `N = p₀ ⋯ p_m`: tuples of candidate Frobenius elements in `A`
whose splitting types are pairwise distinct. -/
def distinctTuples (m : ℕ) (A : Finset G) (T : G → τ) : Finset (Fin (m + 1) → G) :=
  (Fintype.piFinset (fun _ => A)).filter (fun x => Function.Injective (fun i => T (x i)))

/-- The label: the set of factors carrying the smallest splitting type (a singleton on
`distinctTuples`). -/
def minFactor {m : ℕ} (T : G → τ) (x : Fin (m + 1) → G) : Finset (Fin (m + 1)) :=
  univ.filter (fun i => ∀ j, T (x i) ≤ T (x j))

lemma minFactor_comp_perm {m : ℕ} (T : G → τ) (x : Fin (m + 1) → G)
    (s : Equiv.Perm (Fin (m + 1))) :
    minFactor T (x ∘ s) = (minFactor T x).image s.symm := by
  ext l
  simp only [minFactor, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, Function.comp, mem_image]
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨s l, fun j => ?_, by simp⟩
    simpa using h (s.symm j)
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ j
    simpa using hi (s j)

lemma minFactor_singleton {m : ℕ} {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {x : Fin (m + 1) → G}
    (hx : x ∈ distinctTuples m A T) : ∃ i, minFactor T x = {i} := by
  simp only [distinctTuples, mem_filter] at hx
  obtain ⟨i, -, hi⟩ := Finset.exists_min_image univ (fun i => T (x i)) univ_nonempty
  refine ⟨i, ?_⟩
  ext l
  simp only [minFactor, mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and, mem_singleton]
  constructor
  · intro hl
    exact hx.2 (le_antisymm (hl i) (hi l (mem_univ _)))
  · rintro rfl j; exact hi j (mem_univ _)

lemma comp_swap_mem {m : ℕ} {A : Finset G} {T : G → τ} {x : Fin (m + 1) → G}
    (hx : x ∈ distinctTuples m A T) (i j : Fin (m + 1)) :
    x ∘ Equiv.swap i j ∈ distinctTuples m A T := by

  `D4_semiprime_pure_synergy` instantiate these results on the catalog fields.

## Conjectures

### 1. Multi-prime one-time pad with abelian product readout
For `N = p₁⋯p_k` with Frobenius elements i.i.d. uniform on `G`, the coset of
`σ₁⋯σ_k` in `G^ab` shares exactly zero bits with every readout of any `k−1` of the
factors. It shares at most `log₂[G:G']` bits with any readout of all `k`.
*The key insight is* that the shear `(x₁,…,x_k) ↦ (x₁,…,x_{k−1}, x₁⋯x_k)` is a bijection,
so the one-time pad iterates. *Why now?* `card_shear_filter` and the counting form of the
independence law are now in the catalog, so only the induction remains.

### 2. Semiprime completeness criterion
For every finite `G`, coset readout `c` and type readout `T`, with `(σp,σq)` uniform on
`G × G`: `I(c(σpσq); {Tp,Tq}) = log₂[G:G']` **iff** `T` determines the abelianization
coset (`c = φ ∘ T` on `G`).
*The key insight is* that one direction is already close. If `c = φ ∘ T`, the coset of
the product is a function of the ordered pair of cosets, and the general wall
`semiprime_whichFactor_wall_general` moves this to the unordered pair. The converse needs
a fibrewise argument from equality in `mutualInfo_le_left` (`condEntropy_eq_zero_iff`).
*Why now?* The wall, the uniformity of the semiprime residue
(`semiprime_residue_entropy`) and the completeness criterion at the prime level
(`typeChannel_complete_iff`) are all in the catalog. The catalog table is consistent with
the claim: S₃ and S₄ reach the cap, because there the cycle type determines the sign coset. D₄ (≈ 1.430 < 2 bits) and A₄
(≈ 0.474 < log₂3 bits) fall short, and in both groups the cycle type does not determine
the coset.

### 3. Effective transfer to actual primes
Quantify how far the true channel on primes of size X deviates from the uniform-model
values, using effective Chebotarev bounds (unconditional, or under GRH). The goal is to
show that the exact zeros (the one-time pad and the which-factor wall) become o(1)
uniformly in the readout.

### 4. Beyond the abelianization
Characterise the readouts computable from N that are not class functions of σ_pσ_q. Any
surviving method in this family needs a readout of p that, all at once, (i) does not
factor through G^ab, (ii) breaks the p ↔ q symmetry, and (iii) yields more than O(1)
bits about which factor is which. The one-time pad shows that (i) alone is not enough.
